intro.title: How the skills, labels and agent loop fit together
intro.lede: A big idea becomes an initiative of epics. Each epic is briefed, planned into decisions, cut into tickets, built by agents in sandboxes, verified in the running app and merged. Labels on GitHub issues say what each issue is and who acts next. Skills are the commands that move issues along.

principles.title: You decide
principles.body: Scope, the brief, specs and the final merge. Fast and supersonic modes hand some of that to agents.

principles.title: Agents do the legwork
principles.body: Planning on autopilot, building, debugging, reviewing and verifying, in Docker sandboxes.

principles.title: Workflows keep it tidy
principles.body: Triage on every new issue, the epic merge gate, and closing what's done.

flows.title: The fast track
flows.description: The same flow with fast mode on (`AGENTS_MODE=fast`, or the `fast` label on an epic). The loop takes the steps that waited on you: it approves its own spec, answers what's stuck, resolves conflicts and merges the verified epic. You come in only through the dashed arrows, when it asks.
flows.note: Below `AGENTS_THRESHOLD` (70 by default), it asks you instead of deciding. It always asks before spending money, handling real credentials or personal data, deleting or publishing anything.

flows.title: Supersonic
flows.description: Fast mode without the waiting, for throwaway MVPs (`AGENTS_MODE=supersonic`, or the `supersonic` label). `/scope-decomposer` writes every epic's brief in its one interview. Below the threshold, a call that can be undone is assumed instead of asked, and the spec is always approved. The assumptions reach you in one Slack digest a day; comment on an issue to change a call.
flows.note: It still stops and waits for money, credentials, personal data, deleting or publishing: those can't be undone. A wrong guess elsewhere costs rework, since your comment becomes a follow-up ticket. Fine for an MVP; not for production work.

stages.title: Intake
stages.body: Anyone files an issue. Automatic triage labels what it is and who acts next, and comments its reasoning: a small enhancement goes to agents with a brief, a bug to debugging, anything big to scoping, anything unclear back to the reporter.

stages.title: Scope
stages.body: A big idea, yours or a needs-scoping issue, becomes an initiative with epics. Each epic has one destination, one owner area, its own milestone (NN: Initiative / Epic) and branch (epic/NN-slug), and blocking links to the epics it waits on. New products default to a local-first v1.

stages.title: Brief
stages.body: A short, high-level interview per epic captures your must-haves, no-gos and calls already made, saved in the epic's Brief. It ends with your choice: manual or autopilot (and fast, if you want it).

stages.title: Plan
stages.body: Wayfinder charts the decisions an epic needs as tickets and resolves them: with you, one at a time, or alone on autopilot, ending in a spec for your approval. /product-design builds the real UI on mock data until you agree.

stages.title: Tickets
stages.body: The spec is cut into tracer-bullet tickets, each in the epic's milestone with its blockers, labelled for agents.

stages.title: Build & fix
stages.body: The loop picks every ready, unblocked ticket, plans which can run in parallel, and works each in a Docker sandbox: tests first, then a code review. Epic tickets land on the epic branch and close; others arrive as PRs. A ticket it can't finish goes to a person.

stages.title: Verify
stages.body: When a milestone has no open tickets, the loop opens the epic's PR and runs verify-epic in the running app: acceptance criteria, stories, API contracts, agreed screens. Failures become bug tickets, the loop fixes them, and verification runs again.

stages.title: Ship
stages.body: epic-gate turns green when nothing is open, no mocks/ folder is left and verification passed. You merge (fast mode merges for you). The epic closes, then its milestone, then the initiative when it was the last epic.

notes.title: The loop always asks
notes.body: Fast and supersonic modes always stop for you before spending money, handling real credentials or personal data, deleting or publishing anything, or contradicting the brief. They never touch anything labelled `backlog`.

notes.title: Local-first v1
notes.body: For a new product, `/scope-decomposer` recommends building the whole first version on your machine (SQLite or Docker Postgres, local storage, a dev login, console email, test-mode payments). Cloud accounts, domains, secrets and deploys wait in one Go live epic, last and blocking nothing, so the loop never stalls on setup only you can do.

modes.settings: Set the mode in `.sandcastle/.env`: `AGENTS_MODE=fast` or `AGENTS_MODE=supersonic` for a whole project, or label one epic `fast` or `supersonic`. `AGENTS_THRESHOLD` (70 by default) is the confidence below which the loop asks (fast) or assumes (supersonic).
